data.name: AGON - The Lost Sword of Toledo
data.detailed_description:
Professor Samuel Hunt, a historian of the British Museum travels to remote places of the world in search of mystic ancient games, treasured by the last families who can still master them. His current destination is the historic city of Toledo in Spain, famous of traditional sword-making.

On arrival he finds a diseased old friend’s daughter in desperate need of help. She is in love with a young swordsmith who has been jailed innocently for theft of a valuable sword. The Professor soon becomes aware of malicious activities going on behind the scenes. Is it family revenge? Black magic? Lost bet? Dishonest intrigue? He must solve the mystery, as the only way to fulfill his mission is to find the sword and reveal the truth.

Join him now - even if you have not yet played the previous episodes.

Key Features

  • Intriguing plot from an award-winning story-teller
  • Exploration of an authentic, traditional environment
  • Challenging, story-driven puzzles
  • Re-playable ancient board game
  • Amazing graphics
  • Engaging characters and excellent voice acting
  • Rich atmospheric sound, authentic music
  • Suitable for all from 10 to 80++

reviews.review:
Chapter Four--The Lost Sword of Toledo:  After a hiatus of two years, chapter 4 came out.  This is a full game unto itself, about as long as the first three chapter combined.  It should have been shorter, but it really gets bogged down at the start with reading and hearing the background story.  Hardly anything happens that the player can control for a really really long time.  This undoubtedly contributed to its bad reviews, which put the kibosh on any further chapters.  Thus the game ends here, after 4 chapters.  While the story is worthy of an entire film, it is simply too complex for what should have been one chapter of a bigger game.  I see on Steam that some players have put in 100 hours on playing chapter 4!!  If one doesn't use a walkthru in this game, one is doomed to a life of frustration and being stuck in Toledo (Spain).
 
The puzzles are usually way too complicated.  Even the first big one, the music box puzzle, had me scratching my head and using a walkthru (I am a musician).  There are three parts to opening the music box, and all of the solutions are pretty much ridiculous.  There is also a maze in the sewers.  No one likes a maze, yet here it is.  As for the photo puzzle (taking, developing and printing the photo), hours and hours and hours could be spent here experimenting.  This is not fun.  Then comes the big headache, the kaleidoscope puzzle.  It can be skipped over.  Use a walkthru instead.  It's still complicated.  
 
Though seriously flawed, Chapter 4 will provide amusement with a good walkthru.  I liked the graphics and the use of comic book art to fill in transitional passages in the story.  The story was good, too, though it is a long one.  And of course the old professor is one of the better adventure game characters out there.  With reservations (have a walkthru handy) I do recommend the Agon series.  It's an old game, but parts of it are quite good.  I actually won the final board game on my first attempt!  It's unfortunate that the remaining chapters never came out.  However, the professor's great grandson arrived in 2019 with two adventures.  We will eventually give those a try, though being from the same studio I don't hold up too much hope for fair and doable puzzles.
 
Chapter 4 final score:  74%.
